recent_reviews.author: Tony Barlow
recent_reviews.text: I've waited over 3 weeks for a phone consultation despite contacting the surgery because I'm in extreme pain and being told that I would have to have a phone consultation first to be assessed. I've even contacted the surgery a second time to see if the appointment could be brought forward only to be told thar there aren't any other appointments available and that I would have to try ringing at 8am each morning to see if I can get one...a bit difficult when I start work at 7am and drive for a living. Finally got to the day of my appointment only to receive a text message saying that the doctor had tried to get through but couldn't. That's a bit strange because I received the text 5 minutes after I had allegedly been called and also rang the surgery straight back at 16:43 who said the doctor called at 16:28 . Amazing isn't it that I can get through to the surgery but the doctor couldn't get in contact with me when I was in the same location...then again it is getting close to home time after a very long day so why try any harder than you have to. I've now got a appointment with the out of hours doctor in two days time...pity I wasn't offered this earlier. The surgery has gone down the pan and doctors are exploiting the phone consultation.

recent_reviews.author: Roz
recent_reviews.text: 20 years ago Dr Faulkner told me I had IBS without first testing for other causes. Yet on my file it is listed as "suspected IBS" so not formally diagnosed despite being told it was. You cannot diagnose IBS without ruling out other issues. Celiac runs in my family, but it could also be IBD. So been possibly living with either of these untreated for 20 years. Also refused my Right to Choose for ADHD diagnosis (details of which are below, as this was my first reason for the negative review), and had to go private and turns out I do in fact have ADHD. Also failed my Mother in multiple ways, who has now died unexpectedly this year ----- FINAL EDIT: P-UK got in touch personally with Dr Faulkner (only contact they could find) and were ignored. They don't wish to help at all so I'll be switching GP. EDIT: Responded to my letter, basically saying they do not have funding for Bolton, when P-UK have the authority of NHS England that any NHS England patient is eligible for treatment with them under the Right to Choose. I'm now having to follow up. Also, what health centre does not have a way of contacting them online? ----- Really disappointed. Sent a letter to ask to be referred to a specialist (under my Right to Choose) to see if I potentially have ADHD and have had no follow up almost a month later. I'm sure my letter, sent by Signed for Delivery and received, was ignored or thrown away, despite me taking the time to write it and filled in forms which could indicate that I have it and I should be referred. Can't get into the clinic to see someone and ask (though I sent a letter so I'd have some evidence of it). No one has sent a letter or called me. This year has has been extra difficult for me and was hoping I could figure it out so I could get possibly CBT (therapy) to manage it but the clinic do not wish to help. Happy to speak to someone on the phone if they phone me about it, but last time I called about another issue they didn't even know what had happened.

recent_reviews.author: Katie Brett
recent_reviews.text: AVOID AVOID AVOID If I could gove zero stars I would, this has taken a while for me to write. Been with the surgery since birth never changed from the area I live in. I had literally just had a baby and within the first week of giving birth contacted the surgery to register him. Not only was I told this wasn't possible due to my area I was then told I was to find another doctor as I was also out the area due to changes within area restrictions. I explained I had just given birth and had been with them myself for over 30 years to which I was told well I'm sure you will find another doctor, I also explained my concerns over my new babies vaccinations and also his health check an my own, I was told we will send all details over but it can take 8 weeks. I was mortified in tears and emotions all over the place to which I was met with a cold non helpful response an one point a laugh, I didn't find this a funny situation at all I was in a vulnerable position and then had to find myself an my newborn baby a doctor. Also my eldest son was registered with this surgery but at no point was it mentioned he had to be removed it made no sense! I Pleaded to stay with the surgery as I felt comfortable with to be met with we have already removed you whilst on the phone I suggest you find somewhere else. Absolutely disgusting. I removed my eldest son from them as I do not want him to have to deal with surgery and reception staff who work within it. I also accept surgeries have to adhere to changes of area etc but I do not accept how it was dealt with and how I left after just having a baby the most vulnerable position a women could be in! I am so glad I found elsewhere who immediately arranged checks for my baby an myself an ensured all vaccinations where taken care of.

recent_reviews.author: Paul
recent_reviews.text: I feel the need to write this review due to the many unnecessary unfair reviews. I am writing this review to provide feedback on the experiences of my wife, who is a patient at Dr. Subramanian's practice. My wife has been a patient of Dr. Subramanian for many many years, and we wish to convey that she finds him to be an excellent and highly valued doctor. She is more than extremely satisfied with the care she receives and would not consider changing practices. Regarding her access to appointments, my wife has always been able to get an appointment when needed and has never encountered any difficulty in being seen. This is in stark contrast to my own doctors at the same health centre, where it can be impossible to get an appointment unless you book three weeks in advance. Despite the option to call at 8 am for a same-day appointment, I have found it nearly impossible to get through to the practice, which often just gives an out-of-service tone. This brings me to a common complaint I hear from people about potential delays to appointment times. I have observed that Dr. Subramanian often makes a significant effort to accommodate patients who present with urgent issues on the day. Furthermore, I have noticed that delays can also occur when patients require a double appointment but only book a standard one, or they present with multiple issues they need addressing. From what I can see, the doctor is very thorough and compassionate in addressing all of their concerns, which can sometimes extend beyond the scheduled time. While this might occasionally lead to waiting longer for a pre-booked appointment, I believe this reflects a true commitment to ensuring those with immediate needs are seen, and that everyone gets the time they need. This responsiveness for urgent matters is something I value greatly, as it is not always my understanding of how easy it is to access care at other practices. Overall, my wife and I are very happy with the care and accessibility provided by Dr. Subramanian. He is a credit to his profession.

recent_reviews.author: Ellis Birtles
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient at this practice for over 10 years and unfortunately the quality of care has declined significantly. I have been suffering with rectal bleeding and recurrent abscesses for several years, and despite repeatedly asking for further investigation, I have consistently been dismissed. Last week I attended the surgery with heavy rectal bleeding. The doctor would not make eye contact, did not offer a chaperone before asking me to lie on the bed with my underwear down, and carried out no proper examination such as pressing on my abdomen. When I tried to explain my symptoms, I was told to leave the room for being “rude”, even though I was in distress. No help was given, and I was simply told to book another appointment six days later. Because of this, I contacted 111 who sent me to the hospital within an hour due to the seriousness of my symptoms. This is not the first time I’ve had to go through 111 or A&E because the practice would not help. Over the years, my abscesses have repeatedly been dismissed as “boils” and I have only been given mild antibiotics. I have now finally seen a dermatologist who believes my symptoms may be linked to inflammatory bowel disease, something I have been worried about for years but the practice refused to investigate. The reception staff often come across rushed and unfriendly, and I leave most interactions feeling patronised and unheard. Even when I raised my concerns with the practice manager, I felt dismissed again. All I want is to be listened to and to receive proper care. After years of pain, worry, and being ignored, I can no longer trust this practice with my health.

recent_reviews.author: Emma Thornton
recent_reviews.text: I am really disappointed with the service received from this surgery with regards to a private health referral. I am lucky enough to have private health care paid for by my employer, I visited the surgery and asked for a referral from my GP due to the long waiting lists on the NHS. I was advised that I would have to pay £20 for the referral letter, this was because patients with private health care clearly have enough money to be able to afford this charge. May I add I do not pay for this my employer does and why assume I have 'enough' money to fund this. This is absolutely disgusting, I have a £150 excess to pay as part of my private health care, I have opted to use my private insurance to get a quicker appointment and not drain the NHS of valuable resource. I pay my tax and NI every month but opted to not use the NHS saving them potentially thousands of pounds in treatment costs to be told that I need to pay £20 for a standard referral letter to not use the NHS. This is absolutely disgusting service, I would like to know if patients using the NHS who are referred to specialists also have to pay this £20 referral charge.

recent_reviews.author: Rehab Sherif
recent_reviews.text: I had an extremely disappointing experience with this dentist. My appointment was 25 minutes long and I arrived 7 minutes late, due to the car park being full, having to find and pay for on-street parking, and arranging (and paying for) a babysitter to attend the appointment. I explained the situation clearly to the receptionist and asked for it to be relayed to the dentist. Despite this, the dentist showed no empathy or flexibility. After waiting six years to finally register with an NHS dentist since moving to Manchester, I was shocked to be told I would be taken off the register for being late once — something that, having worked in two dental practices myself, I have never known to be standard policy. What made the situation worse was the dentist’s behaviour: instead of speaking to me directly like a professional, he avoided the conversation entirely and hid behind a wall, while incorrectly claiming I was “over 10 minutes late.” This felt dismissive, unprofessional, and frankly inhumane. recent_reviews.text: I have been with this gp since I was 5 im now 22, it used to be good but recently I have been appalled by their actions, I had a cough for about a month and a doctor sent me to the hospital for a chest xray I then had to wait three weeks for that to go back to my doctors. In which time I went back and told a different doctor that it was getting worse he said and I quote "it will go, iv been a doctor for 25 years with people coughing and sneezing on me and I dont get sick, you dont need medicine". So I asked to see another doctor because I wasnt taking his word after what he said I then seen another doctor on the same day and she said my chest sounds crackly, my blood pressure was up and my temp was low, she sent me straight to the ACU ward at the hospital where they did blood and the doctor said there that oh you're fine you can go home. I said to them I dont feel fine its hard to breath and I have asthma at this point im now coughing, fever, sickness, sharp pain in my arm and dizzy. I went home like they said and now on christmas eve all this things have gotten worse and I have collapsed 3 times in 24 hours and I have had an asthma attack. Iv been dealing with this for over three months now and I have been given 2 sets of antibiotics and then taken off them half way through the course. its got to the point everytime I cough I need my inhaler other I will stop breathing its ridiculous and im fuming. The hospital and the doctors say the same thing I dont know what to do im concentrating on making it through a day it feels like they dont care about their patients or what happens to them im seriously disappointed if it turns out that something bigger is going on with me im going to make a complaint and leave.

recent_reviews.author: Sani Vlogs
recent_reviews.text: The reception staff are extremely rude and fail to provide clear instructions when their systems are down. Instead, they assume patients should already know what to do. Communication among reception staff is poor, and speaking through the reception desk does not work properly. As a result, patients are often told “we can’t hear you” in an aggressive manner, rather than the issue being addressed professionally. Even when booking appointments, inappropriate comments are sometimes made when more than one person requires an appointment. In contrast, the doctors are absolutely lovely. They communicate clearly, are respectful, and provide excellent support. Unfortunately, this positive experience is undermined by the behaviour of the reception staff. Reception staff clearly require additional care, communication, and customer service training. Regardless of experience or length of time in the role, rudeness is unjustifiable in a healthcare setting. Professionalism, politeness, and clear communication should be a basic standard at all times.

recent_reviews.author: Nadeem Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: My two young children were unwell, so I booked an appointment Hawthorn Medical walk in centre for 10:00 am. I finished my self-employed work early in order to take them to the surgery and arrived around 9:30 am, hoping to be seen on time. Unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing. The reception staff were rude and appeared completely uninterested. By 10:30 am, I noticed that patients with appointments scheduled after mine were being called in the walking centre (not GP ROOM), while we were still waiting. When I politely questioned this, I was spoken to rudely and told to go to A&E if I was “in a rush”. My children were crying and exhausted, having been unwell and unable to sleep properly all night. I was hoping for some reassurance and relief by having them seen by a doctor. To make matters worse, I overheard a patient with a 10:30 am appointment being taken straight into the walk in doctor’s room, yet my children were not seen until 11:30 am. I cannot understand why this happened. In total, the doctor saw six other patients before finally agreeing to see us, and only after my patience had completely run out as my children were coughing continuously. When we were eventually seen, I received nothing more than a hollow apology. The doctor casually advised me to continue giving paracetamol, despite the fact that my other two children had been prescribed antibiotics for the same condition just two weeks earlier. I felt that the doctor was displeased because I had stood up for my rights, but I strongly believe that had I not spoken out, we may have been left waiting for several more hours. The whole experience was sad and deeply frustrating. This incident makes me seriously question how this surgery has received an “Outstanding” CQC rating.BRIBERY perhaps

recent_reviews.author: Brontë Schiltz
recent_reviews.text: I had a frankly shocking experience at this walk-in centre. I spoke to a nurse called Jackie, who was rude from the outset, challenging my use of the term 'boils' (which is used on the NHS website and was used by a doctor I previously saw about the same kind of infection), then gave me instructions on treating insect bites when the bite I showed her was very clearly infected and my actual reason for calling was that it had transferred to my face, and a boil I had on my face previously became extremely painful and the NHS website says to see a doctor if you get one on your face. She finally agreed to see me after saying that I "clearly wouldn't accept that it was an insect bite" (I never challenged this, just stated that the bite was clearly infected and that I seemed to have spread that infection to my face, which was why I called), and as soon as I arrived, told me that I was overreacting, even denying that the boil on my face was red, hot and inflamed, which it very clearly was. A simple glance at my medical record would show that I have only sought medical attention twice previously since moving to Manchester in 2018, once when I couldn't breathe and once for the aforementioned previous boil, and I waited over a week to seek care in that instance because I have a bit of a phobia of medical settings. I showed her the scars from three previous boils for which I had not sought medical care, and she reluctantly agreed to give me antibiotics but said that I would ruin my immune system if I "kept taking them for things like this", to which I said again that I had not had antibiotics since the first boil on my face around Christmas 2020, and she just sarcastically said "okay". She then gave me a prescription for penicillin, and when I said that I am allergic to penicillin, she challenged this, saying that if all I'd had was a rash then I probably wasn't allergic. I said that I didn't know what my reaction had been since it happened when I was a young child but that it had been diagnosed by a doctor, and she chastised me for not mentioning my allergy sooner, when I had presumably reasonably assumed that it would be on my medical record. She was incredibly confrontational and condescending throughout, insinuating that I was wasting her time when providing healthcare is her job, there was nobody else in the waiting room when I went in, and she saw me 40 minutes after our agreed time, during which I was missing work at my job (at a homelessness charity) which I had to catch up on in my own time. I didn't complain about this because I understand that nurses are very busy, but I didn't appreciate being treated like a hypochondriac when I so rarely seek medical attention and my own time is also valuable. As I was leaving, she again reiterated instructions on responding to bites, which at this point I had stated multiple times was not the reason for my visit. I have a chronic pain condition and do not complain of pain unless it is extremely bad. Hugely disappointing overall.

recent_reviews.author: Polly Williams
recent_reviews.text: Attended this walk in centre with my husband after being advised from our local pharmacy after he had been stung by an insect and had an infected finger. We were going away the next day so didn’t have time to see our GP and didn’t want to waste resources at A and E. The Receptionist very rude when I rang to see if there was availability and abrupt when we arrived and seemed to have a bad attitude.we Waited approx 1.5 hours to be seen. We saw the “Nurse Paula “who was very abrupt and we was in and out within 2 minutes. My husband explained the pharmacist had told him to come as he needed antibiotics as it was Infected. She said it wasn’t infected and “the pharmacist had no right to say we could have antibiotics “ she also commented she would not give us them “ just because we were going away” The following day we travelled to Southampton. My husband developed a rash and became unwell. Again we visited the local pharmacy who said she did not like the look of the rash. She directed us to the local walk In centre. We were seen my friendly helpful staff who took the time to explain about the infection. The nurse requested he was seen by a GP. The GP reported my husband did have an infection and prescribed antibiotics. Such a different experience of two walk in centres. The staff were so much more helpful in Southampton than in our own city of Manchester. If I could award this walk in centre a zero I would.

recent_reviews.author: Russell Lindley
recent_reviews.text: In my experience this is one of the best NHS GP practices in the city, if not the North. It has a functional online booking system in addition to telephoning. The reception staff are generally professional and sympathetic. They have two sites in the city and they are opening a third soon. At some other GP practices in the city, the *only* way to get an appointment is by phoning first thing in the morning and hoping that they still have some slots available. By contrast, at Cornbrook it's usually possible to book routine appointments about 2-4 weeks in advance, and get more urgent appointments much more quickly. All GPs are struggling at the moment because the NHS is underfunded and overstretched in accordance with the government's austerity policies. Most of the negative reviews reflect that.

recent_reviews.author: Mrs Robey
recent_reviews.text: I am sad to have to write this post but after several bad experiences I find I have no option, firstly the on line app, I have on many occasion got up early to be on for 7:00 , to find it not available or to say its now closed, trying to get through on the telephone is a feat in itself, on average it takes between 30 to 80 minutes to get through only to be given incorrect information or told there are no appointments and either ring 111 or try again tomorrow. The latest advice is walk into a pharmacy and get advice from them, on both occasions I have been told they should not be sending adults to pharmacists for the reason I had been sent, and that for many things they can only treat children up to the age of 17. The sad thing is there are good medical staff in the practise and without Janice the practise nurse and the other nurses, the whole place would fall down, I have not been able to see an actual gp at the practise for over 2 years. My advice is better training for the receptionist, as they are constantly giving out incorrect information, you CAN not go to emergency numbers when your own gp is open and you will be told to go back to your gp. The phones need to be manned better or the option to get a ring back rather than kept holding on line. People are genuinely suffering and when you are ill you don't want to be passed around, many people don't have transport to go to these sometimes faraway out of hours practise and if your ill having to go out to appointments late at night in the cold to bolton rochdale or Oldham is barbaric. There is a desperate need for change and maybe invite patients in for a forum to get a clear understanding of how it affects individual patients.

recent_reviews.author: Martin Godfrey
recent_reviews.text: Booking GP appointments at Redbank is done via the AskMyGP website starting at 7am each morning. By logging a request close to this start time i've never had much of a problem getting an appointment over the last four years since they introduced the website. I tend to ring the surgery outside key times (eg after 10am) when booking blood tests and so on. During the pandemic it took a very long time for the phone to be answered, but response times over the last six months have been much much better. It is true that trying to book an appointment over the phone at 8am can be an issue (AskMyGP is the solution to that), but given the number of patients registered at GP practises these days, if each one had 30 receptionists answering the phone at 8am it would likely not be enough. I'd like to thank all the staff for what they do - I've been a patient at the practise for about 10 years now - and have found them universally very helpful.

recent_reviews.author: Katie Spiby
recent_reviews.text: If you see Dr. Flascher I would avoid him if I were you! My dad attended the surgery often, starting in August where my dad suffered pains in his chest. From August to December he seen Dr. Flasher (who isn't his doctor but stands in for him all the time) and over and over he tried to say that my dad had a chest infection and kept giving him various antibiotics. On one occasion when he went in he had seen a nurse who had done his blood and told him he needed to go to the hospital for an X-ray, 24 hours later Dr. Flasher tells my dad OVER THE PHONE he has cancer. My dad was told next month that he had less than 12 months to live, but actually passed away 3 months later. In my opinion Flasher should count his lucky stars my dad didn't take this further with the surgery, as even my dad's doctor said looking at his notes he wasn't happy with the care he received from the surgery. Flasher if you see this I would strongly recommend you should go on further training to look after the patients in your care as I really feel sorry for them!

recent_reviews.author: Mark B
recent_reviews.text: I made a list of other doctors it's easier to book an appointment with: 1. Dr. Dre 2. Dr. Seuss 3. Dr. Joseph Mengele 4. Dr. Martin Luther King 5. Dr Frasier Crane 6. Dr Quinn, Medicine Woman. Being a patient of this surgery is a game of being constantly told to phone back or download the "my GP app" to book a hypothetical callback that never happens, usually when I'm already on the phone to their receptionist, who by default REFUSES to let me see the doctor. I believe this GP is suitably qualified and very competent, but I can't be sure because I've never met him. He/she is 100% the best GP in the world if you enjoy never, EVER being able to make an appointment and being told to call back at narrow windows of opportunity (inevitably when you're at work or competing with every other patient in that small window when they actually answer the phone) . You honestly have more chance of finishing medical school and funding your own private practice clinic than you do getting these people to actually stop obstructing you and let you just see your GP without playing games and messing you around like their time is the only time that matters. Don't believe me? Try and book an appointment with them, just try - I absolutely dare you!

Try and book an appointment with them, just try - I absolutely dare you!Like18 Share Response from the owner 4 years agoThank you again for sharing your experience, Mark and I can see from our records you have now de-registered from the practice, which is unfortunate. I would have liked the opportunity to discuss the issues you raise especially given the length of time you say you've dealt with them on a number of your reviews. Still, hopefully, I can answer some of your queries below. With over 8,000 patients at Uplands and record demand for appointments over the past two years, like all GP practices, we've really struggled, and we openly admit that. When you only have so many appointments you can physically and safely deliver in a day, and demand outstrips supply; unfortunately, that means some patients won't be able to access the care they desperately need. That terrifying thought stays with each and every member of our team as we think of it happening to our own families, I can assure you. At Uplands, our aim has always been to help as many patients as we can, as safely as we can, with the resources we have. We're not a big surgery, but we're big on trying to keep people well, just like Dr Quinn. Staffing issues due to COVID, carefully caring for patients with COVID, staff being drafted in to work on the vaccination programmes, increasing levels of poor mental health amongst patients, long-standing national GP and nurse shortages, not to mention the hospital backlog, which has left many thousands of patients in fear and pain awaiting treatments and consultations...these have left GP practices on their knees. We're so incredibly grateful for the patience and kindness showed to us while we endured the most challenging times ever in primary care, with some sadly still to come, I'm sure. Our reception team are trained to ask patients for a brief outline of their symptoms to inform the GPs. The GPs then assess and decide who needs to be seen most urgently (known as triage), and it works a lot like A&E. If the GP needs to see someone urgently, these are always same-day, by telephone or face to face if clinically appropriate. This continues to be for the safety and care of other vulnerable patients in the building, plus the ability to help as many people as we can in a day. Plus, most patients say it's much more convenient than coming down to the surgery for everything like before and leaving work/school. If the GP decides it's safe to wait a few days, a routine telephone appointment is booked in the first instance. I fully appreciate the frustration of missing a callback. It's happened to me a couple of times with my own surgery. The decision always sits with our clinicians, not the receptionists. I really hope that clears up some of your concerns, Mark and thank you for bringing things to our attention. All the best, Sarah

I'm extremely concerned to read about your experiences, especially regarding the nurse practitioner. I would like to understand more if you have time to contact me to discuss confidentially and directly at: BUCCG.UplandsMedicalPractice@nhs.net We always aim to give excellent service to all our patients and try to demonstrate warmth, care and compassion in all of our interactions so we are saddened to hear of accounts of where our patients do not feel we get it right. Increasingly, in general practice, we have a range of healthcare professionals working with us, which is great as it provides a massive range of skills and specialties within our team. Depending on your symptoms, urgency in the need to be seen and who we have available on the day you call, this might mean you don't always see the same person. We know this can be frustrating for some patients, especially those with long-term health conditions. We will always try to match you with the same doctor or nurse for continuity of care wherever possible. We know this to be an issue on your comments about the building itself. Sadly we are one of hundreds of practices in the region that need updates or new builds, but the national funding just isn't there to support this. Our aim is just to help as many patients as we can, as safely as we can, with the resources we have. I do hope that helps but as I say, I am very happy to be contacted directly to discuss your concerns further. Thanks, Sarah

recent_reviews.text: I had reason to complain to the Practice Manager, Angela, about my elderly mother's monthly prescription, and the problems that seem to occur regularly at the pharmacy. Angela listened to everything I said and promised to investigate. The next day she rang me with the details of what had happened. She did not try and cover up the fact that the surgery staff had been at fault and assured me that she had made it very clear that it was unacceptable that an 86 year old lady had encountered such problems. I found Andrea very helpful, friendly and professional and am reassured that these issues will not happen again. I could not have had a better experience in this case.

recent_reviews.text: Had an appointment today at 11:40 for an ultrasound scan which I had to have a full bladder for. Even though I’m the only one there and have been for the past 35 minutes. She said she’s been calling for me. No one called for me at all whilst I was there. Whatever I was telling her wasn’t going through to her at all. So after sitting there for nearly 45 minutes on a full bladder that I’ve had for 2 hours, I got sent home and a phone call after to re arrange. No thanks I would rather not have the scan anymore to find the issue of what’s making me ill rather than dealing with people like this. And bare in mind whilst I was waiting, one woman kept coming in and out of the room ‘checking around’ but never called my name or spoke to me. Wish I could give this place 0 stars

recent_reviews.author: ENGLISH WITH SABBIR
recent_reviews.text: Terrible Experience at NHS GP Practice The Absolute Worst I am writing this review to express my extreme dissatisfaction with Dr. Parkin's NHS GP practice. This practice is, without a doubt, the worst healthcare experience I've ever had. Here's a list of my grievances: Unbelievably Long Wait Times: Getting an appointment is a nightmare. Even after securing one, expect to wait in the waiting room. Unprofessional Doctors: I've had appointments with various doctors , and none have instilled confidence. They seem unconcerned about my health problems. I would recommend looking for alternative GP practices in the area. There must be better options out there with qualified professionals who genuinely care about their patients' well-being. If you're looking for a GP experience that will leave you feeling more unwell than when you arrived, then NHS is the place for you! Buckle up, because this is a tale of woe. Getting There is an Odyssey: Firstly, reaching a human to book an appointment is an act of pure masochism. The phone lines are permanently engaged in a game of dial tone torture, and the online system is about as user-friendly as a medieval trebuchet. Finally, you're ushered into the office. Prepare for a five-minute consultation. Don't expect in-depth examinations or thoughtful diagnoses. Here, a generic prescription pad are your only companions. I understand that the NHS is under a lot of strain, but that doesn't excuse the unprofessional and unacceptable service.

recent_reviews.author: Carol Laidlaw
recent_reviews.text: I joined this practice about a year ago, I can't comment about Dr Perkins himself because I haven't met him. The only communication I have had with him was indirect, when he told the diabetes practice nurse to tell me he was changing my medication. Communication at one remove like that wasn't sufficient because I had questions about the listed side effects for the new medication (they included increased risk of liver cancer) and I couldn't ask Dr Perkins about them directly. Also, I chose this practice because its website offers booked appointments online, as well as a telephone triage system. That is incorrect, you have to phone at 8 in the morning and hope you can get through in the following five minutes before all that day's appointments are booked up. They refuse to offer appointments booked in advance at all. The effect of that is bound to be that a lot of patients will never be able to get through on the phone and so will effectively be denied treatment. According to the CGC, G.P.s surgeries are supposed to offer more than one method of getting an appointment. I have also still not been given the instructions for how to order repeat prescriptions online, even though I have asked three times. I can only surmise that, however good the doctor is, the practice is being let down by below standard administration. I expect I will only use the practice's services for my annual checks for my existing long term health problems - they are at least efficient at giving me appointments for those - and get treated for any new ailments via the out of hours service. That does give booked appointments. And that being so, I expect I will never actually meet my GP.

recent_reviews.author: Linda Peacock
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient at Edenfield Road Surgery since 1978 and always been more than happy with the care I have received. There have been issues with getting an appointment but I feel that is a problem across the NHS. I find the negative reviews offensive as the staff try their best to accommodate requests in circumstances out of their control. When you see a doctor, pharmacist, nurse practitioner, phlebotomist, nurse or admin staff the service is excellent. I used Patchs today for the first time and had a telephone call from the receptionist within a short time and an appointment with my own doctor, Dr Alam, in the afternoon. His first comment was to remember my husband who passed away in 2022. Dr Alam is very caring and patient as well as being very professional. I always feel I am being listened to as a friend as well as a patient and the appointment is never rushed. I would highly recommend the surgery.

recent_reviews.author: Mike Henry
recent_reviews.text: My wife and I have been patients at this practice for 43 years. The service level dropped dramatically to a point only 18 months ago where one was not treated with respect by reception staff and it had become increasingly difficult to make appointments to see a doctor. This has now changed where the contact between various staff members and myself has noticeably improved. I have had very regular interaction with various doctors, nurses and the phlebotomist over the last year. My health concerns have been both investigated and referrals to specialist centres made very promptly. In particular, appointments with Dr Alam rather than being like a Doctor / Patient one have become like 2 close friends discussing my health. My only reason for not awarding a 5-star review is the ongoing difficulty in obtaining a same day appointment to see a doctor. One rings the practice at 8 am to be told that one is 24th of lower in the queue and then no appointments are available. One way that my wife and I have been able to circumvent this is to go to the practice before 8 am and queue up to make an appointment with one of the reception staff once the practice opens. I am told that from October of this year, one will be able to make online appointment requests from 8 am onwards. In addition, there appear to be a greater number of staff working in the practice - this can only be a positive move in making more appointments available for patients.

recent_reviews.author: Ben Sumner
recent_reviews.text: THE FINAL STRAW - This place is an absolute shambles. One doctor in particular, to mention no names, is incredibly rude and patronising and I have had to make more than one complaint about him in the past. To get an appointment is NEAR impossible - I say near as the receptionist pointed out that 'it's not impossible because you're in aren't you' when I voiced that I have been trying to get in for weeks and therefore wanted to deal with two issues at once (really short issues - a referral and a letter to be sent off. The letter I wanted sending off was because the doctor I previously saw told me I send it off but it should be the surgery so it was their mistake in the first place!) I expressed that I would have to wait weeks to try and get in again and the pedantic receptionist replied 'but you just said it's impossible and it's not is it, because you're in'. This conversation obviously then escalated in an increasingly heated manner. When I tried to calmly voice my frustration she replied in a really rude way 'well if you let me speak but you're not doing'. Not at any point did I speak over her or cut her off. The receptionists need training on how to speak to people calmly when they are upset - because this place is inevitably going to get upset callers. When you ring in the morning BANG ON 8am, it then cuts the phone line off. If you keep trying and you get past around 8am and 30 seconds you've then missed your chance. I went into the surgery to try and set up booking online and had a woman sit with me to explain the process of how to do it through the NHS app. Got up at 6.30am to try it and this didn't work either! When I showed my husband he told me she has set me up on the wrong app! I have anaphylactic allergies and have developed new ones so urgently need testing but when I finally got an appointment with the doctor who is historically rude and having faced this receptionist with a chip on her shoulder, I would rather take my chances with an allergy than step one foot back in this place! With so many negative reviews, this place needs investigating!

recent_reviews.author: Andrew Hopkinson
recent_reviews.text: Appointment booking system is beyond disgraceful. The only people who can get appointments are those who can physically queue outside or are lucky enough to be in the telephone queue within a fraction of a second of the queue opening. As a widower with three school age children (two separate school runs), it is impossible to get an appointment. The online system also fails - the doctors at the practice today decided not to make any online appointments available. This is a highly discriminatory system that needs to be overhauled urgently. How on earth are working single parent families supposed to get to see a GP? There used to be a system in the NHS whereby an appointment was made in the future - an appointment some days away is surely better than the mad scramble that currently exists for telephone or online bookings that can only be made on a day by day basis. Seriously considering changing practice or paying for a private GP's services as my urgent need to see a doctor is proving to be an impossible task. I just hope I don't have a heart attack or stroke before I get to see a GP and three little girls end up homeless and orphaned.

recent_reviews.author: Lisa Cunningham
recent_reviews.text: This is the worse doctors I've ever been registered with. I didn't believe it could be as bad as these reviews. You can not get an appointment even if it's for a baby. They should stop taking on new patients as they they can't cope with the patients they already have registered. Dispite ringing at exactly 8am, you'll be 26th in the queue. You'll wait for nearly an hour for a receptionist to tell you there's no appointments. I tried booking online, as advised by the receptionist, at 6am and 6.30am, but in over a year, I was never been able to get an appointment for myself or my children. I do wonder what medical training the receptionist have as they seem to be acting as the medical professionals at this doctors. I was recently told there was no emergency appointments available for my 9 month old baby and that I shouldn't go to A&E because she had chickpox. I went to the Walk In Centre which was closed. I rang Edenfield Road Surgery again and they refused to give her an appointment. In my desperation I went to a pharmist who told me to go to A&E immediately and that the receptionist advice was completely incorrect. We spent 4 days in North Manchester General Hospital as my baby was very ill. We have now registered with another doctor so that we can actually see a doctor when needed.

recent_reviews.author: Jay Lawson
recent_reviews.text: I work on emergency ambulances responding to 999 calls. On the 4th December 2020 we had a call in for a elderly patient who had fallen and sustained injuries. The patient was unwilling to be taken to A&E Mr Donald Lumb, an Advanced Practitioner at Edenfield Road Surgery. Mr Lumb presented us with several alternative options to A&E, and was knowledgeable of both the resources in the area and the history and preferences of the patient. He even offered to come out immediately to assess the patient. This patient had a really good outcome as a result of the support we received. Thank you Edenfield Road Surgery, Mr Lumb and the secretarial staff who supported us.

They pay more attention to their wickedly long painted nails & miss matched face foundation than the patients genuinely seeking help. The GPs speak to you as they are in a fast forward mode and want to get rid of you as soon as you enter the room. You are made to feel like a burden and come out being more anxious and stressed. Recently I asked for a health questionnaire to be filled out by the GP for the Job purposes. It cost me £8 to get the form printed and handed over to the receptionist in person who said it can take up to four weeks to be completed. Why was I not informed of it when I handed it over to the receptionist or every time I contacted the practice for an update? I wish I could give this practice a negative five rating. I hope someone responsible takes this review seriously and makes sincere effort to turn the place around.

recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient of this practice for over 40 years and for most of those years it was a really excellent family practice but since the retirement of the last of the longest serving GP's 11 months ago the practice has really gone downhill. Unlike previous reviewers I have always found most of the reception staff very helpful and empathetic, particularly given the pressure they must be under in light of the shortage of GP's. The 2 remaining GP's do not have very good people skills and seem more concerned with box ticking paperwork than patient care, Compared to how the practice was run and managed previously the contrast is remarkable and unhappily not in a good way. I have taken the decision to change to a different practice and could certainly no longer recommend this practice to anyone.

When I finally arrived for my appointment, I signed in and waited 40–50 minutes past the scheduled time. I became impatient because the appointment time had clearly passed. I asked the receptionist, who told me to “wait another 5–10 minutes and the doctor will see you soon.” After waiting another 10 minutes, she then told me I needed to come back four hours later at 3:30pm. What a joke. I had children to pick up from school, so attending four hours later was impossible. I asked if I could be booked in for the following week instead, and I was told they had no availability at all for the next two weeks. Completely unacceptable and honestly disgusting. To make matters worse, while I was there another patient was arguing with staff because the doctor refused to see her child despite them having an appointment as well. That alone shows this GP treats multiple patients the same way. This is not the first bad experience either. On previous occasions the staff have been extremely rude. When complaining over the phone in the past, I was told things like: “Why don’t you change GP?” “Why don’t you move out of Oldham?” Disgusting attitude. Completely unprofessional. Shows clearly that this GP surgery does not care at all about its patients. Little Town Medical Practice needs serious improvement. People rely on their GP for their health and wellbeing, and this kind of treatment is shameful. I would not recommend this surgery to anyone.

recent_reviews.author: Aoun Hassan
recent_reviews.text: I’ve never felt so insulted and neglected by a medical professional in my life. Dr. Mahmood’s service was nothing short of appalling. From the moment I walked into the clinic, I was treated with cold indifference and a shocking lack of basic human decency. My health concerns were dismissed like they were a nuisance, and I was spoken to in a tone that was both condescending and careless. It felt like Dr. Mahmood couldn’t be bothered to listen properly, let alone provide any meaningful help. I was rushed, cut off mid-sentence, and treated like just another box to tick on the schedule. The incompetence was glaring – no clear answers, no proper follow-up, and certainly no concern for patient well-being. Frankly, I left each appointment angrier and more helpless than when I arrived. The whole experience was infuriating and demoralizing. I trusted this GP to help me through serious health issues, and instead I was met with arrogance, laziness, and blatant disregard. It’s horrifying that someone with such an apathetic attitude is allowed to practice medicine. I’m beyond relieved to say that I’ve finally switched to a different GP – one who actually listens, cares, and acts like a professional. Dr. Mahmood should be ashamed of the way he treats people. I wouldn’t recommend him to my worst enemy.

recent_reviews.author: Anisa Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: Went today for the second time to book an appt but received an attitude from the receptionists who then walked off without addressing the issue simply because she “does not want to entertain this.” My dad (English is not his first language) tried to go first time and they sent him away with a link to book online. I couldn’t book online after 2pm which is something they had never mentioned but instead said i “went online at the wrong time.” I work a full time job as a doctor with on-call commitments, what’s “the wrong time” sorry? Regardless, I tried numerous times to get him an appt. On walking in today, the receptionist acknowledged he had come before and started to declare his medical situation out loud. I addressed it and said they were breaching confidentiality after which they accused me of being loud and tried to blame me instead. I was very unhappy with the receptionists and told them I would put in a formal complaint. My second concern was, now that they’ve already plastered my dad’s business everywhere, what can we do to avoid this happening with others and suggested maybe go to a separate room and discuss? They weren’t having any of it, she was very rude, tried to conveniently switch the situation onto me and said had we called there wouldn’t be no breach to which I replied there is a subset of patients that cannot use online booking or prefer to come in person for whatever reason (maybe they’re elderly?!). I will put in a written complaint to the practice manager and have changed practices. Please don’t go to this practice. It’s disheartening to see gp receptionists not know of basic NHS principles and maybe we should work on having them trained on medical ethics as well as better triage. At the very least, it is their job to be polite and provide good service to their patients and it is because of individuals like themselves that patients end up not seeing their GPs, fall really unwell and end up at the hospital. I can see why others have left bad reviews in particular because of the receptionists behaviour.

recent_reviews.text: I absolutely Despise this practice, been with them for a decade , so trust me, it’s not one or two incidents It’s a culmination of 10 years of useless service . That excludes how early I always got there I’m trying to have checks to rule out cancer , they never followed up , they said they called back twice - they didn’t ,they rang once for a couple Seconds , where I couldn’t even get to my phone that fast . You can’t return the call and they never followed it up So it was left for me to chase them as always today I finally get in -yet again I’m early and I counted 9 people go in before me despite them appearing to come on time . My brother in law is a paramedic and said it’s important to get checked out , but CH Medical don’t do anything correctly . This is a culmination of a decade of horrific service where they didn’t diagnose my knee properly (for years they got it wrong and a private specialist figured it out in 30 seconds)and , didn’t give a toss when I was in a car accident not of my doing . recent_reviews.author: Jane Williams
recent_reviews.text: I have received an excellent and professional service from all the team members at Chadsfield. I contacted the surgery to make an appointment and the call was answered within a few rings. The receptionist was really helpful and friendly, quickly understood my request for an appointment and that I needed to see a Doctor. She made an appointment for me later that day. I saw Dr Kilroy who carefully listened to what was concerning me and assessed what needed to happened next , making the necessary referral to the relevant hospital department and I was contacted by the hospital and an appointment made with them within a few days. I had another medical issue that was concerning me and Dr Kilrow assessed that and determined I required a further appointment with her and made it there and then . My second appointment was as helpful and professional as the first. Dr Kilroy was friendly , took her time to listen to me and dealt with me in a very professional and compassionate manner. She was very thorough and explained everything to me and made sure I understood what was happening and what the process was and what was going to happen next. I found the whole service and contact with the team at Chadsfield excellent and I thank them for that.,

recent_reviews.author: Dominic Keefe
recent_reviews.text: Some of the doctors here are more thoughtful than others but overall they reflect institutional neglect. I'm dealing with a disabling and frightening chronic condition that has been poorly investigated and diagnosed by the NHS and this health center. Tests have always comeback within their very broad definition of 'normal' and they refuse to apply any further clinical consideration to a patients' actual clinical picture. I asked for my medical records and I still haven't received the requested information three months later. I've complained but received no response. One receptionist a month ago completely ignored me. Then she dealt with me as if it was an inconvenience. The online triage system is now a grim joke. It frequently suspends the option to make an appointment for a week or more, and then every alternative method of contact filters you back to it. The clinic is at the forefront of a modern dysfunctional NHS where compassion disappeared decades ago. The patient comes very last in its considerations and it merely a source of LHA funding. Addendum : I am now discovering that the causes that I suggested for my illness and was laughed out of the surgery with ('Dr' Yazicci actually laughed at them) are indeed the issue and I am now self medicating with considerbale success. The dimissal of my theories by this surgery has cost me years of my life as I didn't act on it. Any attempt to complain to them is water off a duck's back to them. I've since changed surgeries. When I mentioned I was going to this, this one became even less responsive and more dismissive.

recent_reviews.author: First Last
recent_reviews.text: Just had to make a complaint for the first time EVER! I've been waiting MONTHS to get an appointment for plantar fasciitis, and finally had an appointment today, Thurs Sept 18th at 1.30pm. I thought it was at the Bramhall Health Centre close to the centre of Bramhall, and I got there for 1.30pm. Turns out it wasn't, so I have to double back to the very similarly-named Bramhall Park Medical Centre (your texts don't specify the address!) - which is twinned with Shaw Heath, get there for bang on 1.40pm, but I'm only on time to be classed as 'late' and marked down as Did Not Attend. I've rebooked for a couple of weeks from now, but after all this time of waiting, I think this is a DISGUSTING, INTRANSIGENT SYSTEM! Even Michael Douglas in Falling Down only went over 3 minutes at Whammy Burger, but for this, I was late at the precise moment my appointment was cancelled. I did ask if I could still be seen, but Computer Says No. As a result, to say I am ANGRY is an UNDERSTATEMENT! I'll be surprised if anyone cares about this complaint.

recent_reviews.author: Lynsey Hall
recent_reviews.text: Moved to the area in March and filled in all forms in April to be registered. I handed the forms in along with ID etc and rang the following week to see if we was on the system, they said "no ring again in another week or so". My 2 year old had a very bad chest and I called them again to be told I'm still not on the system and had to call 111 instead. After being in a cue of 30 people I decided to walk down to the surgery and ask them face to face to be told they have no records at all and our paper work is lost! I was really upset by this as not only are forms time consuming this is also a Data Protection issue. I reluctantly filled in New forms and returned them a few days later, my husband was in bed ill with a bad chest so I handed them in myself and asked them if they can put us on the system this time please, my husband needs to see doctor. She said she can't not unless he was there in person, which i understand but he's ill they could have made an exception. I told her to hand me the forms back and that I do not wish to be registered with them, its been nothing but hard work and the service has been very disappointing. I have now found a new doctors who don't loose private and confidential information. If you want your data protected don't go here.

recent_reviews.author: Sandeep Tandon
recent_reviews.text: I ordered my repeat prescription via the app several days ago. When I attended the pharmacy, I was told the prescription had not been authorised by the doctor. On Thursday, I attended the surgery and was informed by the receptionist that the particular doctor was “not in”. I explained the urgency and asked for the prescription to be pushed through. I was then assured that my medication would be ready to collect from the pharmacy on Saturday morning. Today (Saturday 17/01/26), I attended the pharmacy at 1pm, only to find that it was closed. Both the pharmacy and the GP surgery are now closed. As of today, I have completely run out of my prescribed medication, including Ramipril and Atorvastatin. I have disabilities and suffer from high blood pressure, and being without this medication places my health at risk. I am extremely concerned that the online prescription service is being promoted, yet it is ineffective if prescriptions are not authorised in a timely manner. The system only works if doctors take responsibility for approving patients’ medication. I would like this matter urgently reviewed, an explanation provided as to how this situation was allowed to occur, and assurances that this does not happen again. I also request immediate advice on how I can obtain my medication as soon as possible. I look forward to your prompt response. Yours faithfully, S
